payload.title: [sfu-media-6] No mediasoup worker 'died' handler — a crashed worker leaves all routers silently dead
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING sfu-media-6 (medium/stability, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/calls/mediasoup-sfu-backend.ts
LINES: 280-297, 117-150

WHAT: #startWorker creates the worker but never subscribes to its 'died' event (rg for .on(/died/observer in the file is empty). mediasoup workers are separate C++ processes that can crash; the canonical guidance is to listen for worker.on('died') and rebuild. Here, after a crash #worker still references the dead handle, ensureRouter returns it, and all subsequent createRouter/createWebRtcTransport calls fail (or hang) while #routers still holds entries pointing at a dead worker. The backend never self-heals and never surfaces the death.

IMPACT: On worker crash the SFU silently stops forwarding media for every call on the node with no recovery path and no signal — a node-wide media outage masquerading as healthy until each operation fails. Routers/transports tracked in #routers become orphaned references.

SUGGESTED FIX: Attach worker.on('died', ...) in #startWorker: log (without PII), drop #worker/#workerInit and the now-dead #routers entries, and surface/raise so callers re-allocate. Consider rebuilding routers for live calls.
